output.proposal: HB No. 10688 seeks to create the Health Procurement and Stockpiling Bureau (HPSB) under the Department of Health (DOH) to serve as the principal agency for DOH procurement and for stockpiling, conserving and releasing life-saving drugs and medicines, vaccines, devices and materials during public health emergencies. It also establishes a Medical Stockpiling Fund sourced from donations and grants.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine whether creating the HPSB, which under Section 5 (Organization) absorbs the existing Procurement Service and Logistics Management Division of the DOH, results in a net expansion of the bureaucracy or a reorganization of existing units, and how its procurement and supply-chain functions under Section 6 (Functions and Responsibilities) fit with those of existing procurement and health bodies, consistent with the government's intent to streamline agencies and reduce overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly its focus on the Universal Health Care system. No corresponding measure is identified in the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda.
legislative_history: HB No. 10688 was filed on August 10, 2026 by Representative Alfred Delos Santos; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not reflected in the available records.
Near-identical measures were filed in the same Congress: HB No. 4110 and HB No. 10732.
Closely matching measures were filed in the 19th Congress: HB No. 284, HB No. 4153 and HB No. 7247.
Measures with the same title were filed in the 18th Congress: HB No. 6995 (filed June 15, 2020) and HB No. 9456 (filed May 25, 2021, pending in the Committee); their texts were not reviewed.
No substitute bill, committee report or Senate counterpart is identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 10688 seeks to establish the Health Procurement and Stockpiling Bureau (HPSB) under the DOH to centralize DOH procurement and to maintain a stockpile of strategic and critical drugs and medicines, vaccines, devices and materials for public health emergencies. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 2 (Declaration of Policy) provides that the State shall protect public health by preventing and controlling the spread of diseases through the stockpiling of essential and critical health commodities.
b. Section 4 (Creation of a Health Procurement and Stockpiling Bureau) provides that the HPSB is created under the DOH as the principal agency for DOH procurement and for stockpiling, conserving and releasing life-saving health commodities during public health emergencies.
c. Section 5 (Organization) provides that the Bureau shall absorb the Procurement Service and Logistics Management Division of the DOH, with the Secretary of Health determining its organizational structure and staffing modifications subject to DBM approval; no head, positions or salary grades are specified.
d. Section 6 (Functions and Responsibilities) provides that the Bureau shall formulate procurement plans and policies, undertake procurement under the Government Procurement Reform Act, identify strategic and critical commodities, maintain a buffer supply, and act as supply-chain manager for stock rotation and replenishment, among others.
e. Section 7 (Sources) provides that commodities may be obtained from domestic or foreign sources, with the Bureau encouraging domestic sources, including through countertrade and industrial cooperation.
f. Section 8 (Industrial Collaboration Program) provides that the DOH shall maintain partnerships with government agencies, international organizations and civil society on the procurement, distribution and use of stockpiled commodities.
g. Section 9 (Establishment of Medical Stockpiling Fund and Tax Exemptions) provides that donations, grants and fund-raising proceeds shall form a Medical Stockpiling Fund supporting the National Drug and Device Security Program, with tax exemptions and deductibility for donors, and cash receipts recorded as a special account in the General Fund.
h. Section 10 (Report to Congress) provides that the DOH shall submit an annual report to the House and Senate health committees on stockpile purchases, acquisitions and disposals.
i. Section 11 (Appropriations) provides that initial implementation shall be charged against the DOH's current-year appropriation, and thereafter included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
j. Section 12 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides that the Secretary of Health shall issue the implementing rules within sixty days from effectivity.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 10688 may be considered alongside HB No. 4110 and HB No. 10732 of the 20th Congress, which propose near-identical measures, and builds on earlier versions filed in the 19th Congress (HB No. 284, HB No. 4153 and HB No. 7247) and same-titled bills in the 18th Congress. The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, particularly the Universal Health Care system. The review should assess whether converting the existing DOH Procurement Service and Logistics Management Division into a bureau under Section 5 (Organization) entails additional positions and costs, how the Bureau's functions relate to the Price Negotiation Board under Section 28(b) of RA No. 11223 as referenced in Section 8 (Industrial Collaboration Program), and whether the creation of a new bureau is consistent with the streamlining objectives of the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231).

reviewer_checks: Section 3 (Definition of Terms) defines countertrade as transactions of at least One million dollars but gives the figure as US$1; confirm the intended amount.
Section 9 (Establishment of Medical Stockpiling Fund and Tax Exemptions) refers to a National Drug and Device Security Program that is not established elsewhere in the bill; confirm its basis.
Section 8 (Industrial Collaboration Program) contains a typographical error in the name of the Department of National Defense.
Section 5 (Organization) does not specify the head of the Bureau or its positions and salary grades; confirm the staffing and cost implications with the DOH.
Section 1 (Short Title) uses the title Health Procurement and Stockpiling Act of 2026, while the related bills omit the year; confirm the intended short title.
Confirm the current status of HB No. 4110 and HB No. 10732 with the House of Representatives, and whether a consolidation is being considered.
